capability: Shipment received by another person: the order's shipment is received by someone other than the buyer, a delegate assigned to receive it, whose details the store's invoice can show in place of the order's owner (Zid: shipment receipt by another person / عرض خيار استلام الشحنة من شخص آخر, shipment_receipt_by_different_consignee; Salla: المستلم المفوض, delegate)
note: Made by the coordinator from the held pass (held/new.tsv, 31 October; held/new-proposals.md, N05), in M-amend. Its place of its own: Zid's plan policy orders_and_products_specifications.shipment_receipt_by_different_consignee, 'Show feature for shipment receipt by another person.' (other-product-class@0d79b794f:zid/structures/store-plan-policies/items.jsonl line 340, ZD-11:122), a policy in the plan's own list. Salla's is one switch of its invoice settings, which shows the delegated recipient's details in place of the order's owner, 'في حال تعيين مستلم مفوض لاستلام الطلب' (SA-26:146, SA-27:17), not a place of its own. Joined, a reading: the same thing on both platforms, as SA-26 already read it; how a delegate is assigned isn't stated. Not gifting (CM-LOY-006): nothing says the other person isn't the buyer's agent (ZD-11's notes). Its parent is the shipping setup, by the coordinator's decision: Zid keeps the policy under Orders and products properties and Salla its switch in the invoice settings, so neither platform's grouping decides it; CM-CHK-009, an option at checkout, is the alternative. No platform's concern-map statement holds it: every cell is none-held, and held_amend.py adds Zid's and Salla's held lines.

capability: Order limits: a minimum or a maximum that a buyer's order must meet, on its value or on its quantities (Zid: minimum order limit, maximum order limit / تفعيل حد أدنى للطلب, تفعيل حد أقصى للطلب, min_limit_for_order, max_limit_for_order; Shopify: Quantity rules, minimum order quantity, maximum order quantity, Add-to-cart limit; Salla: تخصيص الطلبات (حد أدنى))
note: Made by the coordinator from the held pass (held/new.tsv, 31 October; held/new-proposals.md, N06), in M-amend. Its place of its own: Zid's two plan policies orders_and_products_specifications.min_limit_for_order and max_limit_for_order, 'Enable minimum order limit' and 'Enable maximum order limit' (other-product-class@0d79b794f:zid/structures/store-plan-policies/items.jsonl lines 338 and 339, ZD-11:120, ZD-11:121), policies in the plan's own list. Whether Zid's limit is on an order's value or on its quantities isn't stated, so the capability holds either. Joined on role, a reading: a minimum or a maximum an order must meet. Shopify's Quantity rules set 'minimum, maximum, and increment quantity rules for product purchasing' in B2B catalogs (SH-41:190), and its Add-to-cart limit sets 'how many of each product a customer can add to their cart in one order' (SH-C-046/reason/SH-S-7489); Salla's plan line names a minimum, حد أدنى, among its customizations of orders (SA-C-002/decides/SA-S-2097), whose unit isn't stated either. Not CM-ORD-010's daily order limit, a count of the orders the store accepts, nor CM-CHK-005's app-written validation (ZD-11's notes). Its parent is the cart, by the coordinator's decision; CM-B2B-003 is the alternative for Shopify's quantity rules, which are set in catalogs.

capability: Tipping: the buyer adds a tip to the order, as a percentage of its total or a custom amount, at the online checkout or at the point of sale (Shopify: Tipping, tipping options, Tips, Collect tips)
note: Made by the coordinator from the held pass (held/new.tsv, 31 October; held/new-proposals.md, N10), in M-amend. Its places of its own: the checkout settings' anchor Tipping, with its own title and path, 'Show tipping options at checkout' (observed-sh@e38dc17e3:structures/shopify/admin-router/items.jsonl line 358, SH-10:78), and the POS app's settings item Tips and its page, with the switch Collect tips (observed-sh@e38dc17e3:structures/shopify/pos-settings/fake-demo-sharrwah/items.jsonl lines 52 and 191, SH-96:31, SH-96:59): an anchor the manifest names within a route, with its own title and path, is a place of its own (B-extent, Q3M-6). The tip is 'based on a percentage of their total order or a custom amount' (SH-45:17). Shopify only so far: Salla's, Zid's, WooCommerce's and BigCommerce's statements hold none, in English or, for Salla and Zid, Arabic. Its parent is checkout, where Shopify's settings put it; CM-POS-001 stays beside the POS lines (held/new-proposals.md).

note: Made by the coordinator from the held pass (held/new.tsv, 31 October; held/new-proposals.md, N11), in M-amend. Its place of its own: Shopify's plan feature 'Fraud protection and 3D Secure checkout', a line of the plan's own list (observed-sh@e38dc17e3:structures/shopify/pricing-page-data/20261031T003815Z-shopify-com-pricing-by-country/items.jsonl line 85, SH-75:185). No capability held card authentication. Joined across Shopify and BigCommerce by the name of the scheme, 3D Secure, which both name (SH-C-186/boundary/SH-S-6071, BC-C-022/reason/BC-S-0130), a reading. BigCommerce's statement is cited on CM-PAY-022 too, for the stored payment instrument; the proposals give it as the lead for its cell here. The changelog digest's C46.4 placed Shopify's 3D Secure, then a setting inside Shopify Payments with no place of its own, on CM-PAY-002 core and on CM-PAY-009 core for its stated effect on chargebacks (held/rules/merchant-changelog.md; held/shopify/notes-SH-46.md, entry SH-E-747ee5be): now that 3D Secure has a capability, whether those lines move here is the coordinator's. Its parent is the store's payment settings, by the coordinator's decision.
